market.title: Make a market
market.question: What is this hand worth, and how sure are you?
market.intro: Two poker hands are dealt face up. You quote a price on hand A, and a trader decides whether to take the other side. A game is five hands.
rules: Hand A’s fair value is its share of the pot, out of 100, averaged over every way the rest of the board can come. A win counts 1 and a tie counts a half. Ace-king of spades against two red queens before the flop is worth 46.2.

You quote a bid and an ask. The trader sells to you at your bid if they think the hand is worth less, and buys from you at your ask if they think it is worth more. Sell above fair value or buy below it and you make the difference. The other way round, you lose it.
One trader in three is sharp and knows fair value exactly. The rest are guessing.
Quote too wide and nobody trades. Quote too tight around the wrong number and the sharp trader takes your money.

formula.expression: belief = fair value + ε,  ε ~ N(0, 8²)

market.note: A stylized game: one trader and one contract per hand, no fees.

invite.question: Want to play a market-making game?

steps.title: Two hands, face up
paragraphs: Hand A’s fair value is its share of the pot, out of 100, averaged over every way the board can finish. Ace-king of spades against two red queens is worth 46.2.

steps.title: You quote two prices
paragraphs: A bid you would buy at and an ask you would sell at. Here the market is 40 to 52.
In the game you only see fair value after you quote.

steps.title: A trader answers
paragraphs: They buy at your ask if they think the hand is worth more, and sell at your bid if they think it is worth less. This one thinks 58.
One trader in three knows the exact value. Quote too wide and nobody trades. Quote too tight around the wrong number and the sharp one takes your money.

about.label: Who I am
paragraphs: I’m studying applied math at UC Berkeley. I’m into quant, AI, and modeling. I chose it after going into math and finding I was at least decent at it, and I knew it was what I wanted to do. I love the stock market too.
I’m outgoing, and I’m devoted to doing my best at whatever I take on. I made this site so that someone curious about the same things can see how I went about a project and try something similar.

about.label: How I got here
paragraphs: I went to Palmdale High School, in its Engineering Academy, and took community college classes alongside it. I entered Berkeley with 45 college credits.

In 2025 I was a MITES Semester scholar. One of my first projects was a poker equity simulator I built there. It made a question that felt intuitive into something I could actually compute. Since then I’ve used simulation to explore market risk, worked with three robots to study crowding, and built an educational health model that shows the range of outcomes its assumptions can produce.

outside.title: Health
outside.text: My favorite way to train is full body, every other day, and I care about what I eat. I love kiwis. In high school I swam varsity.

outside.title: Faith
outside.text: Faith is a big part of who I am. From 2025 to 2026 I helped run sound for weekly services at my church, with about 150 people in the room and about 300 on the livestream.

outside.title: The shop
outside.text: In 2022 I started a resale shop with $25 and filled more than 600 orders. I’m not running it anymore, but I loved it, and it gave me a reason to build small tools I’d actually use.

outside.title: Quant
outside.text: I love quant. I started studying NQ and ES futures on my own in 2021, and the research workbench grew out of that.
